title: Farrell 2015 schizophrenia candidate-gene review: historical candidate literature against GWAS-era denominator evidence
summary: A meta-research audit record for schizophrenia candidate genes. It compares the pre-GWAS candidate-gene literature, meta-analytic evidence, PGC GWAS results, and expert assessment, preserving both the negative conclusion and the historical “set the stage” nuance.

status_history.note: The seed flags candidate-gene-era psychiatric genetics as a deep subcorpus.
Promoted in rev0018 candidate-gene / GWAS denominator lane.

time.evidence_context: pre-GWAS candidate-gene literature evaluated in light of PGC/common-variant GWAS evidence available by 2014/2015

subjects.name: SZGene meta-analysis plus PGC GWAS/mega-analysis evidence

claims.claim: Farrell et al. state that, before the GWAS era, candidate-gene studies were a major approach in schizophrenia genetics; the SZGene database listed 1,406 candidate-gene papers investigating more than 700 genes.
what_would_change_status: A corrected version of the review changes the SZGene count or scope.

claims.claim: The review evaluated 25 historical candidate genes through meta-analysis of candidate-gene data, PGC schizophrenia mega-analysis results, informed-investigator ratings, and survey ratings from schizophrenia geneticists.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass review shows the method summary omits a material evaluation surface.

claims.claim: The review concludes that current empirical evidence did not support the idea that the historical candidate-gene literature produced robust, replicable genetic findings with etiological insight; the likely reason includes grossly inadequate statistical power, but the authors preserve a qualifier that knowledge remains incomplete.
what_would_change_status: A later review of the same 25 genes finds strong replicated evidence materially changing the conclusion.

claims.claim: The review is not a blame record: it says early candidate studies were not unreasonable given prior tools and that their efforts set the stage for current genomic approaches to schizophrenia.
what_would_change_status: A future historical review materially revises this “reasonable at the time / stage-setting” interpretation.

limitations: Does not encode every gene-level conclusion.
PGC 2014 schizophrenia paper not promoted separately in this revision.
Expert-rating surfaces are only summarized, not reconstructed.

type_payload.denominator_surface: SZGene meta-analysis surfaces, PGC schizophrenia GWAS/mega-analysis results, and expert assessment surfaces described by Farrell et al.
type_payload.numerator_surface: historical candidate-gene findings, reviews, and individually plausible gene hypotheses from pre-GWAS schizophrenia genetics
bias_mechanisms_encoded: post-hoc survival of famous gene narratives
limits: Not every candidate gene is individually refuted forever.
Rare variation and CNV findings require separate records.
The review explicitly leaves room for future evidence and notes early studies helped stage current work.

handling_notes: Do not portray the field as foolish; record the change in tools, thresholds, and denominator size.
Avoid psychiatric stigma and genetic determinism.

unknowns: PGC schizophrenia 2014 primary paper and 2022 updates not promoted separately.
No ancestry-diversity record specific to schizophrenia yet.
next_actions: Add child records for COMT, DISC1, NRG1, DTNBP1, DRD2/GRM3 if useful.
Add PGC schizophrenia primary GWAS records and later locus-count updates with strict temporal status.
Add positive-control candidate gene success records before claiming a general “candidate genes fail” pattern.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: historical literature composition not fully extracted
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: do not infer GWAS finality or no rare/structural genetic contribution
